crossReferences.gist: The stale-manifest sync in T-26443 is a consequence of the RFC's push-to-stage mode: the external promoter has not moved fresh manifests, so auto-sync deploys whatever the stage branch last held.
The CI diff failures in T-26271 track the impersonation RFC: with the flag on, operations run as the destination service account, not the broad cluster-secret credential the reporter is inspecting.

The delete/re-create loop in T-28511 interacts with the PRD's reverse deletion strategy: the strategy waits for full deletion before advancing, and a stuck Progressing resource means the wait never completes.

conflicts.gist: The strategy doc rules out ordered/automated deletion of ApplicationSet children (teardown stays manual); the PRD promises exactly that ordered automated deletion.

risks.gist: Combining the impersonation RFC's narrow destination service accounts with T-28695's evidence that server-side diff demands patch authority on every resource type: rolling impersonation out fleet-wide silently breaks diff wherever the service account is scoped tightly — which is the whole point of the feature.

Combining the hydrator RFC (every hydration cycle lands a new commit on the deployed-from branch) with T-27949 (progressive sync restarts its wave on source change): on hydrated repos, rollout waves restart every hydration cycle and large rollouts may never complete.

expectedProposals.gist: Record the root cause on T-26271: with impersonation on, diff runs as the destination service account lacking patch on cluster-scoped resources.
Note on T-27327 that hydrator history & rollback is deprioritized to next quarter.

findings.gist: The hydrated branch attributes authorship to a human name copied from the dry commit while the only mechanism that could prove or disprove that attribution, commit signing, ships opt-in and defaults to off, leaving a provenance record that cannot be verified.
Committing the application-controller pair to close out Progressive Sync's Stable-promotion punch list this quarter is the reason controller sharding has no one staffed on it until that list closes.

The PRD promises Reverse deletion's determinism rests on rollingSync.steps staying a strictly sequential list, while the parallel-steps proposal commits to step groups evaluated concurrently, where match groups inside a group have no relative order to reverse.

The stabilization ticket records a freeze on the rollingSync.steps shape once Progressive Sync goes Stable, which forecloses the parallel-steps proposal's in-place restructuring of that same field unless it lands first, and neither ticket cross-references the other.

keywords: specChanged|stuck sync|without a resulting sync|no sync operation
findings.gist: The ticket asserts a specific incidence rate for the specChanged-without-sync bug, but the progressive-sync metrics ticket shows no counter exists that could confirm or refute any such rate, so the number is unfalsifiable.

The commit-server RPC locks its fields as proto2 required, so when the rollback flow becomes the service's second caller it must supply values for fields designed only for fresh hydration commits, a mismatch the wire contract can never relax.

The fail-fast single signing key crash-loops the commit server fleet-wide behind only a generic pod-health alert, and because the notes record the downstream stage-branch promoter as having no owner, nobody's job is to notice the resulting promotion stall either.

The rollback flow's push bypasses the commit server, so on a branch requiring verified signatures the push is rejected and the operator is left at a failed-push message with no explanation of the cause and no recovery path in the interface.

The signing key that backs SourceIntegrity verification is mounted in the shared control-plane namespace rather than the isolated namespace the hydrator design recommends, so anything with Secret-read reach there can produce commits the verification step treats as authentic.

roleFindings.replanted: 2026-08-10 (third entry), committed before any run is scored against it. Nine plants authored to the rule that a discriminating plant is keyed to the territory its owning lens UNIQUELY asks about, not to a kind of finding: strategy owns displaced work, product owns a promise made twice, program owns a restriction blocking a different workstream, architect owns what becomes hard to undo, operations owns how anyone finds out at 3am, design owns where a person gets stuck, security owns what someone gains, analyst owns what cannot be observed, legal owns who authored a record and what binds the organization. CP1 is unchanged because it already discriminated, and it is the model for the rest. Known risks recorded BEFORE scoring rather than discovered after: five of the nine sit on the manifest-hydrator and commit-signing material, so a run that sweeps that area may earn several; L2 and TH3 share a document pair and are separated only by their term sets; and C2 and TP2 both bear on the parallel-steps proposal from different pairs. Whether these hold is what the next sweep measures.
